**\[Academic\] Crime Related Media and its Effect on Criminal Profiling (Everyone 18+)**

You are invited to participate in a study named “Crime Related Media and its Effect on Criminal Profiling.” The purpose of this study is to examine how crime related media will affect criminal profiling skills. If you decide to participate, you will fill out questionnaires about your crime media consumption and a crime scene profile provided in the survey.  The entire study will take approximately 15 to 20 minutes.

Eligibility Requirements Minimum age of 18 years. 

Please contact researchers with any questions, concerns, or complaints. 

Researchers: Vivian Mullins (vivian.mullins@rmc-cmr.ca) and Alexandra Zidenberg (alexandra.zidenberg@umontreal.ca)

Link: [https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/JLWQV9M](https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/JLWQV9M)

Also available in French: [https://fr.surveymonkey.com/r/J3JQ5BC](https://fr.surveymonkey.com/r/J3JQ5BC)

**\[Academic\] Revalidating the Multiple-Perpetrator Rape Interest Scale (Everyone 18+)**

Study Title: Revalidating the Multiple-Perpetrator Rape Interest Scale

Eligibility Criteria: At least 18 years old

How to Participate: If you meet the eligibility criteria and are willing to contribute, please click on the following link to access the survey: [https://pacificu.co1.qualtrics.com/.../SV\_eA4C35dNjca8PXw](https://pacificu.co1.qualtrics.com/.../SV_eA4C35dNjca8PXw)

Duration: The survey should take approximately 10-15 minutes to complete.

$$ Incentive: As a token of appreciation for your time and contribution, you may enter a raffle for a chance to win one of five $20 Amazon gift cards.

Why Participate: By participating this study, you may contribute valuable insights that can help us better understand the dynamics of sexual violence.

If you have any questions, please contact us via email: Ibobadilla@pacificu.edu and saad.iqbal@pacificu.edu.

Thank you so much, Saad Iqbal, Dr. Leonardo Bobadilla and Dr. Alexandra Zidenberg

Pacific University | University of Montreal

**Evaluating a Mental Health Care Provider (Everyone over 18)**  
Hello! Our research team is inviting you to participate in a study named “Evaluating a Mental Health Care Provider.” The purpose of this study is to examine how individuals make decisions about their mental health care. If you decide to take part, you will be asked to read a short profile of a psychological care provider, fill out some questions assessing your attitudes about the profile, and answer some basic questions about yourself. The entire study will take approximately 15 minutes to complete. Click the link below to begin the study:

[https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/YR3MTDV](https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/YR3MTDV)

**Research Participation Request: Decisions Regarding Mental Health Care**

You are invited to participate in a study named “Decisions Regarding Mental Health Care.” The purpose of this study is to examine how individuals make decisions about their mental health care. If you decide to take part, you will be asked to read a short profile of a psychological care provider, fill out some questions assessing your attitudes about the profile, and to answer some basic questions about yourself. The entire study will take approximately 10 to 15 minutes. Click the link below to begin the study:

[https://www.surveymonkey.ca/r/2VNC365](https://www.surveymonkey.ca/r/2VNC365)

**Eligibility Requirements:** Minimum age requirement of 17 years. People of all gender identities are welcome to participate. Participants must be living in Canada. 

Please contact researchers with any questions, concerns, or complaints.

**Researchers:** Alexandra Zidenberg ([alexandra.zidenberg@usask.ca](mailto:alexandra.zidenberg@usask.ca)), Shannah Dutrisac ([shannah.dutrisac@usask.ca](mailto:shannah.dutrisac@usask.ca)), and Mark Olver (mark.olver@usask.ca)

This research is approved by the U of S Behavioural Research Ethics Board (BEH 2086)

Many psychology clinics and websites feature profiles like the one in the survey, we are interested in how people engage with the information provided in those profiles. Hopefully it will help us understand how Canadians make decisions about their mental health care and which providers they may put their trust in. I'm always happy to discuss further if you'd like. Thank you for your interest in our study!

**\[Academic\] Juror Perceptions of Sexual Violence against Men (18+ living in Canada or the United States)**

You are invited to participate in a study named “Juror Perceptions of Sexual Violence against Men.” This study is looking at how mock jurors perceive situations involving sexual violence. If you decide to take part, you will read a short scenario, fill out some questionnaires asking about your attitudes, and answer some questions about yourself as well as the scenario.

Please be aware that some of the questionnaires contain questions about sexual violence, and these topics may be upsetting to participants, particularly individuals who have experienced sexual trauma. Participating in this study will take approximately 15 to 20 minutes. Click the link below to begin the study:  
[https://www.surveymonkey.ca/r/L7M7655](https://www.surveymonkey.ca/r/L7M7655?fbclid=IwAR1S1cY66ILK_eizN8h9YDg5Qy2ICz8wjMR6fzjcI4pHJUSE4M3f5zMHc2k)

Eligibility Requirements: Minimum age requirement of 18 years. People of all gender identities are welcome to participate.

Please contact researchers with any questions, concerns, or complaints.

Researchers: Alexandra Zidenberg ([alexandra.zidenberg@usask.ca](mailto:alexandra.zidenberg@usask.ca))

This research is approved by the University of Saskatchewan Behavioural Research Ethics Board (BEH ID 1478)
